resolutions.watched_red: Before any fix, on the reviewed HEAD: 'fenced reject + trailing prose' want {verdict: FAIL, responsive: false, attempts: 1, calls: 1, judge_tokens: 7} / got {verdict: PASS, attempts: 2, calls: 2, judge_tokens: 14, responsive: true}; 'leading prose + fenced reject' and 'bare reject + trailing prose' identically PASS/2/2.
resolutions.fix: Replaced wrapper-stripping with a scan. `_json_objects` walks the body with json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode and returns every top-level JSON object, skipping to each object's end index so a nested object is not counted twice. Bare, fenced, one-line, leading prose, trailing prose all read the same bytes the same way. Zero objects is the unreadable class and the ONLY retryable one; two or more is ambiguous ('the schema is {...}, my answer is {...}') and fails closed on attempt 1 rather than being picked by position. The fence strip and the now-unused `re` import are deleted.
resolutions.rationale: Three rounds of the same defect (one-line fence, then fullmatch fence, then this) is a signal that predicting wrapper shapes is the wrong mechanism, not that the prediction needed another patch.
resolutions.ablations: Both new guards ablated to prove they can go red: removing the ambiguity check and removing the nested-skip each redden the case to 58/59. The implementer reported that its FIRST nested-skip ablation was a silent no-op (wrong indentation in the patch string, matched nothing, reported green), caught and redone. Recorded because a green ablation is exactly what must not be taken on trust.
